definitions.E6:
Yes—there’s one active biochemistry-related program:

**Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science** — Bachelor of Science, full-time, in person at Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)
definitions.E4:
There are **two admission pathways**:

- **UBC pathway:** eligibility for the honours specialization, a minimum **76% GPA** (**70% for September 2026**), 8 credits of UBC Chemistry—**CHEM 121, CHEM 111, or CHEM 141 Principles of Chemistry**, plus **CHEM 123 Principles of Chemistry 2**—along with **BIOL 112 Biology of the Cell**, 3 credits meeting UBC’s Communication Requirement, and 3 credits of differential calculus.
- **Transfer pathway:** two terms of Chemistry with labs, plus one term each of Biology, English, and differential calculus.

A criminal record check is also an entrance requirement, but its timing needs confirmation. Since you haven’t shared your academic background, I can’t yet determine which requirements you meet.

[View the program and admissions information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)
definitions.E1:
Graduation requires **132 credits** across the four-year UBC/BCIT curriculum:

- Year 1 UBC: **34 credits**
- Year 2: **9 BCIT + 24 UBC credits**
- Year 3: **18 BCIT + 15 UBC credits**
- Year 4: **11 BCIT + 21 UBC credits**

Key required choices include:

- One of **MATH 100, MATH 102, or MATH 104 Differential Calculus**
- One of **DSCI 100 Introduction to Data Science** or **CPSC 103 Introduction to Systematic Program Design**
- One of **STAT 201 Statistical Inference for Data Science** or **CPSC 203 Programming, Problem Solving, and Algorithms**
- A Year 4 route: **BIOC 449 Honours Thesis** plus 3 advanced-biochemistry elective credits, **or** **BIOC 420 Advanced Biochemical Techniques** plus 6 such elective credits

The curriculum also includes required biochemistry, biology, chemistry, forensic-science, communication, and LIBS 7020 — Bioethics courses. The exact Year 3 forensic-elective selection rule isn’t specified in the stored curriculum.

[View the complete graduation curriculum](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)
definitions.E5: Three credits from the required alternative set DSCI 100 or CPSC 103; required for graduation, not admission. Neither course is individually mandatory; an institution-approved transfer or equivalent may satisfy the requirement.
